INCIDENT INC-2026-041
Service: Payment API
Severity: Critical
Symptoms: 503 errors, database connection timeout, payment transactions failing
Error Rate: 87.0%
Deployment Version: v2.4.1
Context: Spike in traffic after marketing campaign, connections not being released properly
Root Cause: Database connection pool exhaustion due to connection leak in async handler introduced in v2.4.1
Resolution: Rolled back to v2.4.0, restarted services, temporarily increased pool size. Root cause: missing await on connection.close() in new async payment handler.
Runbook Used: payment-db-recovery
Recovery Time: 8 minutes

POST-MORTEM for INC-2026-041
Service: Payment API
Root Cause (confirmed): Connection leak in async payment handler introduced in v2.4.1 — missing await on connection.close()
What Happened: After deploying v2.4.1, async payment handlers started accumulating unclosed connections. Under normal traffic this was masked, but the marketing campaign spike exposed the leak causing pool exhaustion within 12 minutes.
How It Was Resolved: Immediate rollback to v2.4.0, service restart, temporary pool increase to 200. Fix: added proper async context manager for all DB connections in new handlers.
What Did NOT Work: Initially tried increasing pool size without rollback — insufficient fix
Successful Runbook: payment-db-recovery
Recovery Time: 8 minutes
Lessons Learned: All async database handlers must use context managers. Pre-production load testing should simulate peak traffic. DB pool metrics must be in alerting.
Preventive Actions: Added DB connection count to PagerDuty alerts. Code review checklist now requires async context manager review. Load testing pipeline added to CI/CD.

INCIDENT INC-2026-018
Service: Payment API
Severity: SEV-1
Symptoms: High latency, intermittent 503 errors, DB query timeouts
Error Rate: 34.0%
Deployment Version: v2.3.0
Context: Occurred during database maintenance window
Root Cause: DB connection pool misconfiguration after infrastructure upgrade — max_overflow too low for new server capacity
Resolution: Increased max_overflow from 10 to 100, matched to new DB server capacity
Runbook Used: payment-db-recovery
Recovery Time: 22 minutes

POST-MORTEM for INC-2026-018
Service: Payment API
Root Cause (confirmed): Connection pool max_overflow setting not updated after DB server upgrade
What Happened: DB server was upgraded to a larger instance but application pool settings remained at old limits, causing pool overflow during normal traffic
How It Was Resolved: Updated max_overflow from 10 to 100 in application config. Deployed config update without service restart.
What Did NOT Work: Attempted service restart before finding root cause — extended downtime
Successful Runbook: payment-db-recovery
Recovery Time: 22 minutes
Lessons Learned: Infrastructure changes must be accompanied by application configuration review. Pool settings should be proportional to DB server capacity.
Preventive Actions: Created infrastructure change checklist that includes application config review. DB pool settings now documented in runbook.

INCIDENT INC-2025-092
Service: Auth Service
Severity: Critical
Symptoms: Login failures, JWT token validation errors, 401 responses across all services
Error Rate: 100.0%
Deployment Version: v1.8.0
Context: Occurred after scheduled secret rotation
Root Cause: JWT secret rotation deployed without grace period — old tokens invalidated immediately causing 100% auth failure
Resolution: Rolled back secret rotation, implemented dual-key validation, planned gradual migration over 24h
Runbook Used: auth-jwt-recovery
Recovery Time: 15 minutes

POST-MORTEM for INC-2025-092
Service: Auth Service
Root Cause (confirmed): JWT secret rotation mechanism did not implement token migration grace period
What Happened: Scheduled secret rotation immediately invalidated all existing tokens, causing 100% authentication failures across all services that relied on auth service
How It Was Resolved: Emergency rollback of secret, temporary dual-key validation added. Full rotation completed over 24 hours with grace period.
What Did NOT Work: Initial attempt to force re-login all users failed due to volume
Successful Runbook: auth-jwt-recovery
Recovery Time: 15 minutes
Lessons Learned: Secret rotations must always include grace period for existing tokens. Never use hard cutover for JWT secrets in production.
Preventive Actions: Auth runbook updated. Dual-key validation now built into rotation process. Staged rollout added for secret changes.

INCIDENT INC-2025-071
Service: API Gateway
Severity: High
Symptoms: Rate limiting errors across all services, upstream timeout failures
Error Rate: 45.0%
Deployment Version: gateway-v3.2.0
Context: After scaling up backend services
Root Cause: API gateway upstream timeout too short after backend services scaled up — new instances took longer to warm up
Resolution: Increased proxy_read_timeout from 30s to 120s, added 60s slow-start for new pods
Runbook Used: gateway-timeout-recovery
Recovery Time: 35 minutes

POST-MORTEM for INC-2025-071
Service: API Gateway
Root Cause (confirmed): Default upstream timeout insufficient for larger backend instances that require longer JVM warm-up time
What Happened: During a scale-up event, new JVM-based service instances were added to rotation before completing warm-up. Gateway timeouts to these cold instances caused cascading failures.
How It Was Resolved: Increased upstream timeout, added slow-start configuration for new instances, implemented readiness probes.
What Did NOT Work: Rolling back scaling operation worsened load on existing instances temporarily
Successful Runbook: gateway-timeout-recovery
Recovery Time: 35 minutes
Lessons Learned: JVM services require warm-up period before taking traffic. Readiness probes must be configured for all services. Slow-start should be default for scale-out events.
Preventive Actions: Added readiness probes to all JVM services. Slow-start now configured in service mesh. Scaling playbook updated.

INCIDENT INC-2025-055
Service: User Service
Severity: SEV-2
Symptoms: User profile updates failing, 500 errors, database write timeouts
Error Rate: 28.0%
Deployment Version: user-service-v4.1.0
Context: Running bulk migration job alongside production traffic
Root Cause: Database deadlock between bulk migration job and production write operations on users table
Resolution: Killed migration job, waited for deadlocks to clear, rescheduled migration for 2am
Runbook Used: db-deadlock-resolution
Recovery Time: 18 minutes

POST-MORTEM for INC-2025-055
Service: User Service
Root Cause (confirmed): Bulk migration job ran concurrently with production traffic without proper locking strategy
What Happened: A bulk user data migration job was initiated during business hours. The job held row-level locks that conflicted with production write operations, causing cascading deadlocks.
How It Was Resolved: Terminated migration job, waited for deadlock resolution, verified data consistency, rescheduled migration for off-peak hours with proper rate limiting.
What Did NOT Work: Tried to pause migration instead of stop — insufficient, deadlocks continued
Successful Runbook: db-deadlock-resolution
Recovery Time: 18 minutes
Lessons Learned: Bulk data operations must never run during business hours without proper lock management. Migration jobs should use advisory locks and rate limiting.
Preventive Actions: Created production change policy requiring off-peak for bulk operations. Added migration job to maintenance window scheduler.

Resolution: Restarted service, queries normalized within 5 minutes
Recovery Time: 12 minutes

INCIDENT INC-2026-7086C5
Service: Payment API
Severity: Critical
Symptoms: Complete payment service outage, all transactions failing
Resolution: Rolled back deployment, services restored
Recovery Time: 15 minutes

POST-MORTEM for INC-2026-7086C5
Service: Payment API
Root Cause (confirmed): Memory leak in new async payment handler introduced in latest deployment
What Happened: Service ran out of memory under load, causing OOM kills
How It Was Resolved: Rolled back to previous version, memory stabilized
Successful Runbook: payment-db-recovery
Recovery Time: 15 minutes
Lessons Learned: All deployments must include memory profiling under load. OOM alerts must fire earlier.
Preventive Actions: Added memory usage to deployment health gates
